OPENED AND HELD, AND THE IDENTIFICATION METHOD IS SOUND. The 15-parameter init is a genuine one-for-one twin and I walked it slot by slot: web §1t99s0§.as:185-199 vs android MCSPlayer.as:184-198 - controlledBy, setHP, maxhp, setChi, maxchi, defense, baseReload, minDamage, damageRange, baseSlashLength, slashUsage, lightMastery, balancedMastery, heavyMastery, level, in that exact order with no gaps. §1t4478s0§ at web :3293-3298 is deductReloadBar at android :3240-3245 statement for statement ('if(this.reload == this.maxreload) { this.reload = 0; }' then the same x0.5 / x1 / x1.5 per-stance drain), which fixes §1t4414s0§ = reload and §1t4415s0§ = maxreload beyond argument. new_findings.text: TWO UPHELD FINDINGS CANNOT BOTH BE TRUE, AND THE FREE-SWITCH ONE IS WRONG. LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:943, [[combat-core/the-in-combat-stance-gate-is-reload-48-of-a-192-max]] (UPHELD, 4 critics, web v0.717), asserts 'the in-combat stance switch costs no Focus and no Chi: it needs the reload meter at 48/192 = 25%.' At least five other UPHELD findings assert the opposite flat -48 cost (LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:285, :606, :710-712, :718-724, :1993-1995). I opened the code. The cycle body §1t99s0§.as:3058-3080 - the only range that finding cites - indeed contains no debit: it gates at :3060 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48) return;' and then calls this.§1t3489s0§(...) at :3070 / :3074 / :3078. The debit is one function further down, inside §1t3489s0§ (setStance) at :3160-3166: 'if(§1t1525s0§.§1t9948s0§()) { this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48; if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 0) { this.§1t4414s0§ = 0; } }', where §1t9948s0§ is isBattle (§1t1525s0§.as:1152-1155, §1t9903s0§ = 2 at :53, matched to android StageManager.as:1027 STATE_BATTLE). The android twin makes the same debit at MCSPlayer.as:3096-3105 with different constants. So the in-battle switch BOTH requires 48 and spends 48 on a 192 meter (§1t99s0§.as:249 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;'): four switches from full, not unlimited switching above 25 percent. The defect is a truncated read, not a build-parity artefact - both builds charge. The rewrite must delete the 'costs no Focus and no Chi' clause from that banked finding while keeping its gate number, which is correct.

new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core + L2 skills-meters: the stance rule is gate >= 48 AND spend 48 on RELOAD_MAX = 192. Strike the 'costs no Focus and no Chi' clause from [[combat-core/the-in-combat-stance-gate-is-reload-48-of-a-192-max]] before the rewrite reads it; keep its 48/192 gate. Without this the rewrite picks one of two upheld findings at random and ships a stance system that is either free or priced.

new_findings.text: THE 300/200/100 CROSS-CHECK IS A BUILD-PARITY TRAP AND THREE UPHELD FINDINGS EACH GET A DIFFERENT ANSWER FROM IT. All of them agree the triple is a MASTERY-ZERO row rather than RR:155's 'MASTERY-9 CEILING', and that conclusion is safe. What they disagree on is the base. [[combat-core/300-200-100-is-base-not-ceiling]] gets it EXACTLY, from android arithmetic: InputManager.as:51 'internal static var maxDistance:int = 200;' times the android mastery-0 multipliers 1.5 / 1.0 / 0.5 (MCSPlayer.as:3030, :3041, :3052) = 300 / 200 / 100 to the digit. The two web-side findings in my packet cannot reach it, because web Light is 1.4 not 1.5 (§1t99s0§.as:3094): one takes a 210 px base and reports 294 / 210 / 105, the other takes a 214 px base and reports 300 / 214 / 107 and calls the 214-vs-200 gap 'rounding' - it is a 7 percent miss. The base cannot be moved to make all three terms land, because the web ratio is fixed at 2.8 : 2 : 1 while the wiki triple is 3 : 2 : 1. CONCLUSION: the wiki triple is reproducible only under v0.682 coefficients against the InputManager DEFAULT (which is a static initialiser overwritten by setMaxDistance on every setStance, so it is a fallback, not a player value). A v0.717 target must take the formula (base = 120 + floor((90 + DAN*5) * SPD_eff / (20 + SPD_eff)), stance x1.4 / x(1+0.02m) / xmax(0.5+0.04m, 100/base)) and must NOT use 300/200/100 to validate it.

new_findings.text: RR:155 IS ONE SENTENCE CARRYING TWO TABLES THAT NEED OPPOSITE CORRECTIONS, AND THE REWRITE WILL PICK ONE. 'The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.' Both halves are wrong in DIFFERENT directions and both fixes are already upheld. DAMAGE half: 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.4 IS a ceiling row - it is just labelled one rung low. §1t99s0§.as:3262 gives Light dmg x(0.5 + 0.4*lightMastery*0.1), :3265 Balanced x(1 + 0.2*balancedMastery*0.1), :3270 Heavy/Dual/Reversed flat x1.4; at mastery 10 that is 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.4 exactly, and strings.json["8131"] 'Light Stance Mastery Level 10.' fixes the cap at 10. So the damage half needs MASTERY-9 -> MASTERY-10. REACH half: 300 / 200 / 100 is not a ceiling at all - the reach multipliers run the OTHER WAY (§1t99s0§.as:3094 Light x1.4 flat, :3105 Balanced x(1 + 0.02m), :3116 Heavy x(0.5 + 0.04m)), so their ceiling is 1.4 / 1.2 / 0.9, which cannot produce a 3 : 2 : 1 shape off any base. The reach triple is a MASTERY-ZERO row. So the damage half must be re-labelled UP a rung and the reach half must be re-labelled DOWN to zero, in the same sentence. A writer who applies [[cite-s27b/stance-damage-ceiling-is-mastery-10-not-mastery-9]] deletes the reach fix; a writer who applies [[combat-core/300-200-100-is-base-not-ceiling]] or either finding in my packet deletes the damage fix. The sentence must be SPLIT INTO TWO before either correction lands.
new_findings.ledger_text: 3. **The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.**
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core: split RR:155 into a damage sentence ('dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4 is the MASTERY-10 ceiling; mastery 0 is 0.5/1.0/1.4') and a reach sentence ('reach 300/200/100 is the MASTERY-0 row; the mastery-10 reach ceiling is 1.4/1.2/0.9 of base'). Damage and reach scale in OPPOSITE directions with mastery and must never share a sentence again.

new_findings.text: THE GAME'S OWN 'slash distance' READOUT AND THE ENGINE'S LIVE REACH DISAGREE AT LOW SPEED, AND THE UPHELD CORPUS TREATS THEM AS THE SAME NUMBER. The engine clamps: §1t99s0§.as:3116-3119 sets Heavy reach to base*(0.5 + 0.04m) then 'if(this.§1t4417s0§ < 100) { this.§1t4417s0§ = 100; }', and :3142-3145 does the same for §1t12223s0§. The stats panel does not: §1t5957s0§.as:3013 prints 'int(_loc21_ * _loc48_)' where _loc21_ is §1t9593s0§(...) (:2719) and _loc48_ is the raw stance multiplier (:2729 / :2738 / :2747) - no floor anywhere in that block. Android is identical: InventoryUI.as:2232 'str += "slash distance: " + ... int(baseSlashLength * slashModifier) ...' against the floored MCSPlayer.as:3052-3055. Concretely, a fresh v0.717 character (DAN 0, SPD 1) has base = 120 + floor(90*1/21) = 124, so in Heavy at mastery 0 the panel reads 62 while the engine actually gives 100 - a 61 percent understatement, and the panel only stops lying once base*(0.5+0.04m) clears 100. This matters because the 'slash distance' readout is the artifact the reach-close leans on to prove the unit; it proves the unit, but it is NOT a safe source for the value.
new_findings.build: web v0.717, confirmed by the android twin
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core + L8 ui-hud: config takes reach = max(base * stanceMult, 100) for Heavy and Dual, but the stats panel must render the UNFLOORED product to be 1:1. Two constants, not one. Any lane that tries to validate the reach formula against a filmed stats panel will read the wrong number below base 200 in Heavy.

new_findings.text: THE STAGE-PX-TO-FRAME-PX CONVERSION THE CORPUS USES IS RIGHT ON ONE AXIS ONLY. Two upheld findings convert the recovered reach into screen pixels at 'x2.4 screen px per stage px in a 1080p capture' (LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:3084 and :3370), from the stage width. I opened the constants on the WEB side, not just the android side: §1t1523s0§.as:104 'public static var stageWidth:int = 800;' and :106 'public static var stageHeight:int = 480;' (android StatsManager.as:80, :82 identical). 800 x 480 is 5:3. A 1920 x 1080 capture is 16:9. 1920/800 = 2.40 but 1080/480 = 2.25, so no single uniform scale maps the game stage onto a 1080p frame - the capture is either width-fit and vertically cropped or overflowed, or height-fit at 2.25 and pillarboxed. InputManager.as:223-224 confirms a runtime scale exists and is applied as '(args.stageX - StatsManager.stageOffsetX) / StatsManager.stageScale', with an offset on both axes, i.e. the game explicitly supports letterboxing. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: RR:190 blocker (1) asked for the reach 'in stage px' precisely so it could be checked against footage. The formula is recovered, but the last step - stage px to frame px - is being done with a factor that cannot be right for both axes, and a blade path is drawn diagonally, so it uses both. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED: which fit the two longplays used. That needs one frame (A1) measuring a known-width stage element, and I did not open one.
new_findings.quote: §1t1523s0§.as:104 'public static var stageWidth:int = 800;' · :106 'public static var stageHeight:int = 480;' · InputManager.as:223 'mouseX = (args.stageX - StatsManager.stageOffsetX) / StatsManager.stageScale;'
new_findings.build: web v0.717 (android v0.682 carries the same two constants)
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core + L-art-anim-feel: do NOT bank 'x2.4 screen px per stage px' as a conversion. Bank the stage as 800 x 480 with a runtime stageScale + stageOffsetX/Y, and open ONE frame to settle whether the longplays are width-fit (2.40, cropped vertically) or height-fit (2.25, pillarboxed) before any reach number is graded against footage.
